# Roadmap

- `/orchestrate` is the only lifecycle entry point, and it is token-cheap by construction: delegate, read back compact verdicts, ask the user only when a decision is genuinely the user's. `MAX_TASKS` is 8, enforced in `commands/orchestrate.md`.
- Counts and rosters are generated (`generate-task-order.sh --print`, `roadmap-integration.sh --regenerate`, `orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh --next-batch`). Never transcribe one here. As of 2026-11-11: **137 open (2 held), 5 awaiting `/todo` archival**.

<a id="milestone-m3"></a>
## M3: Batch worktree isolation off a per-batch branch

Run each batch in its own worktree off its own batch branch so concurrent dispatches cannot collide over one working tree.

- **Progress**: planned -- no batches yet -- Every member is held and sited in no batch; the /slice ruling finds isolation irrelevant to review, pending an operator decision.
- **Review**: none
- **Gate**: A batch runs in an isolated worktree off its batch branch; a partial batch retains its worktree and /refresh reports it as an orphan; and every remaining project-root consumer is classified code-root, state-root or both, with the write-time and git-guard hooks honouring that split.

## M2: Sapience linked projects, capture activation and collaborator access

Make a repository bindable to a shared Sapience project and workable by a second person: bind and register the repo, resolve every automatic write and read through the link, let extension activation alone decide capture, and keep the token out of the MCP entry.

- **Progress**: active -- 1/2 batches, 5/6 tasks done -- Link, policy and token work landed; capture coupling then collaborator setup remain.
- **Review**: none
- **Gate**: A collaborator with their own account and a plain Claude Code install goes from a fresh clone of a linked repo to a verified project note without help; every automatic write and retrieval resolves the linked project rather than a directory-name label; loading or unloading the extension is the only switch over a repo's capture; no registered MCP entry carries the Sapience token.

<a id="roadmap-context"></a>
## Rules, conventions and repo context

### Rules

- **Agent-system defects get filed here.** A fix in a consuming repo's `.claude/` is wiped on reload.
- **`.claude/**` is a deploy artifact.** Edit `agent-system/extensions/**`, then resync. `settings.json` and `settings.local.json` are **install-once** — copied only when absent; put hook registrations in a fragment surface (decision 18).
- **`TODO.md` is generated from `state.json`.** Edit `description` via `state-write.sh`, then `generate-todo.sh`. Same for this file's counts and rosters — generate them.
- **Propose, then apply, across repos.**
- **Verify by execution, not by reading.** Re-measure before acting. *CARRIED-UNVERIFIED* figures must be re-derived.
- **The lead never reads a report, plan, summary, description or context file during the loop.**
- **This file describes the current plan only.** No revision history, no pass numbers.
- **A scope cut justified by an unverified premise is not a scope cut.** Test the premise before dropping the work it would make unnecessary.
- **A redundancy census is re-derived, never remembered.** Fan-out, unordered-overlap counts and duplicate readings all change with every edge and every closure. Compute from `state.json` plus `scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh` with transitive closure as the ordering test.
- **Work held by operator direction is sited in no batch.** `/orchestrate` refuses a held task, so siting one renders a command an operator cannot run as printed. It stays visible under *Open tasks in no batch* with its `HOLD` token until the hold lifts.

### Conventions

- `orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh --dry-run --state-file specs/state.json <tasks>` — space-separated. Admits what you expect; `md5sum specs/state.json` unchanged.
- `validate-state.sh --deep` — measure before your work too; today's baseline is 0 failed, 8 warnings (2026-11-11).
- `verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow` — before and after, and compare. **Never concurrently with the battery.** A standing red is not permission to ignore a new one.
- To tell a working dispatch from a stranded one, read artifact mtimes and live child processes. Absent `.orchestrator-handoff.json` is NOT a stall signal — research never writes one.
- Edges go through `state-write.sh`, acyclicity confirmed afterwards by `validate-state.sh --deep`. `--depends-on-add` cannot reach a `not_started` task, and there is no edge-removal flag at all.
- If a dead owner holds `specs/.gate-lock`, release it by its own token (`task-lock.sh gate-release <token>`). Gate 8 now traps `INT`/`TERM`/`HUP`, so only `SIGKILL` leaks it, self-healing after 1800 s.
- **Batch of one.** One engine; single-task is a batch of one. Team mode deleted; hard mode kept, per-invocation.
- **The orchestrator never asks and never decides.** Only an agent-surfaced `user_decision` reaches the user, once, at cycle end. `blocking: false` proceeds on the agent's recommendation.
- **Research-first is the default** for a fresh task; `--fast` restores planner-first.
- **`--dry-run` prints the plan it would dispatch.** No separate dry-run report.
- **No fixed consumer validation gates.** The checks above are recommended, not blocking.
- **A linear chain of small tasks serializing on one file is one task with phases** — at creation time, and applied late when it was not.
- **`file_scope` warnings are live input.** In-batch collisions block, cross-batch are advisory. Decision 17 does not weaken this: an *unordered* overlapping pair shares a wave and writes concurrently.
- **Rule before mechanism** for the vimtex hazard.
- **Skeleton plans terminate through the completion-claim gate.** No `pr_ready` outside `type=pr`.
- **No third automated deploy-trigger site.** Exactly two: `command-gate-out.sh` + `orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh`, per `test-lint-deploy-caller-wrap.sh`.
- **One grant mechanism.** A single-use token bound to action, remote, branch and sha, minted only where the harness can prove the user typed it. Nothing the model writes is a grant. PR/MR creation and `/merge` stay user-only.
- **A grant may authorize a plain push of the default branch.** Every force form on the default branch, bare `--force` anywhere, and all bulk/deletion refspecs stay excluded, checked before any grant lookup.
- **`known-failures.txt` is the only known-failing list.** Advisory; never changes which suites run. Never keep a prose copy elsewhere. A `needs-owner` row is a known gap owed a follow-up task. **Shell suites only** — plenary Lua specs have no baseline at all.
